meta.settingGenerator: node:crypto randomInt (plan built once, CSPRNG-shuffled, stored in meta.plan)
meta.planDoc: Phase C: 200 bets = 4 epochs × 50 on risk low, 1 spot (a CSPRNG sample of 0..39 per bet), stake 100 × the minimum; the config with the highest probability of a non-zero payout in the hbverify paytable: P = 1 (tie with medium/1, broken by the lower payout variance); P(payout > stake) = 0.25

body.derivation: block_i = HMAC_SHA256(key = serverSeed, message = clientSeed:nonce:i). Ball i of a round (i = 0 … 9) is bytes 4i..4i+3 of block_0 ‖ block_1 read as a big-endian number u; it is the number at position floor(u × (40 − i) / 2^32) among the numbers not yet drawn, kept in ascending order — the same as floor(float × (40 − i)) with float = Σ byte_j / 256^(j+1), the derivation public Keno calculators use for 40 numbers and 10 draws.
body.tiles: Numbers are the tiles 0 to 39 from left to right, top to bottom, shown as 1 to 40.
rules: pick 1 to 10 numbers and a risk (classic, low, medium or high) before the bet; the ten numbers drawn are fixed by the seed pair and the nonce at the bet
ten different numbers are drawn; the bet pays by how many of the picks are among them, from the paytable of the risk and the number of picks
a payout is the stake × the multiplier, rounded down to the wallet's smallest unit (1e-8) once
a stake whose top prize (every pick drawn) would pay more than the max win above it is refused before the draw
the round settles in the request that places it: there is no round to leave open
body.return: 99% at every risk and every number of picks, to within one millionth: each paytable is solved so that Σ P(hits) × multiplier is at most 99/100 and at least 99/100 − 1e-6, with P(hits) hypergeometric on 40 numbers and 10 drawn
body.summary: block_i = HMAC_SHA256(key = serverSeed, message = clientSeed:nonce:i). Ball i of a round (i = 0 … 9) is bytes 4i..4i+3 of block_0 ‖ block_1 read as a big-endian number u; it is the number at position floor(u × (40 − i) / 2^32) among the numbers not yet drawn, kept in ascending order — the same as floor(float × (40 − i)) with float = Σ byte_j / 256^(j+1), the derivation public Keno calculators use for 40 numbers and 10 draws. Numbers are the tiles 0 to 39 from left to right, top to bottom, shown as 1 to 40. The game returns 99% at every risk and every number of picks, to within one millionth: each paytable is solved so that Σ P(hits) × multiplier is at most 99/100 and at least 99/100 − 1e-6, with P(hits) hypergeometric on 40 numbers and 10 drawn. The server seed is committed up front by its SHA-256 hash and revealed when you rotate the pair, so every draw is fixed before the bet and can be checked afterwards.
